reference: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert sunlight into chemical energy. Chlorophyll in the leaves absorbs light. Water is drawn up from the roots. Carbon dioxide enters through small pores called stomata. The resulting glucose fuels the plant's growth.
summary: Plants use sunlight to make food. Leaves absorb light and roots supply water. This is called photosynthesis, which means making things with light.

reference: The central bank raised interest rates by half a percentage point on Wednesday. Officials cited persistent inflation as the primary driver. Markets had largely anticipated the move. Analysts expect further tightening later this year. Consumer borrowing costs are likely to rise.
summary: The central bank raised interest rates by half a point to fight inflation. Borrowing will get more expensive and more increases are expected.

reference: A new study published in the journal Nature examined coral reef recovery after bleaching events. Researchers tracked forty reefs over a decade. Reefs with diverse fish populations recovered faster. Water temperature remained the strongest predictor of decline. Conservation zones showed measurable benefits.
summary: A decade-long study found that coral reefs with more fish species recover faster from bleaching. For example, protected zones did better. Warmer water was the biggest threat.

reference: The committee reviewed the proposed zoning changes for the downtown district. Several residents voiced concerns about increased traffic. The developer presented a revised parking plan. A vote was postponed until the next session. Additional environmental review was requested.
summary: The committee looked at downtown zoning changes. Residents worried about traffic, so the vote was delayed pending more review.

reference: Regular physical activity reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease. Even moderate exercise such as brisk walking provides benefits. The heart becomes more efficient at pumping blood. Blood pressure tends to decrease over time. Doctors recommend at least 150 minutes of activity per week.
summary: Exercise, even brisk walking, is good for your heart. It lowers blood pressure and makes the heart stronger. Aim for 150 minutes a week.

reference: The software update introduces end-to-end encryption for all messages. Users must verify their identity with a one-time code. Older devices may experience slower performance. The company says the change protects user privacy. A rollback option is available for administrators.
summary: The update adds end-to-end encryption, which means only you can read your messages. You verify with a code. Old phones may run slower.

reference: Archaeologists uncovered a well-preserved Roman villa near the coast. The site includes intricate mosaic floors and a private bathhouse. Pottery fragments suggest continuous occupation for two centuries. The find sheds light on rural life in the province. Excavation will continue through the summer.
summary: Archaeologists found a Roman villa with mosaic floors and a bathhouse near the coast. Pottery shows people lived there for 200 years.

reference: The airline announced it would cut several regional routes next quarter. Rising fuel costs and weak demand were blamed. Affected passengers will be offered refunds or rebooking. Union representatives criticized the timing. The company maintains the cuts are necessary for profitability.
summary: The airline is cutting regional routes because of high fuel costs and low demand. Passengers get refunds or rebooking, but the union objects.

reference: Scientists have developed a biodegradable plastic derived from seaweed. The material breaks down within weeks in seawater. It could reduce ocean pollution from packaging. Production remains more expensive than conventional plastic. Trials with food packaging are underway.
summary: Researchers made a seaweed-based plastic that breaks down in seawater within weeks. It could cut ocean pollution, but it costs more to make right now.

reference: The museum unveiled a restored seventeenth-century painting after two years of conservation work. Experts removed layers of yellowed varnish. Hidden details in the background became visible. The artist's original palette was far brighter than assumed. The work returns to public display next month.
summary: A museum restored a 1600s painting over two years. Removing old varnish revealed hidden details and brighter original colors. It goes back on display next month.
